rule: Every row separates current best answer from what remains unproved. Parent-owned answers move the question upward; they are not rewritten as OCM novelty.

questions.question: Does a unique irreducible cognitive atom exist?
questions.current_best_answer: Do not assume uniqueness. Exact Boolean calibration already demonstrates multiple syntactically distinct minimal generating bases in a toy function class; general intelligence may likewise have equivalence classes of bases.
questions.next: Stage-C adaptive-basis census plus bounded mutual-compilation relation.

questions.question: Is minimality absolute?
questions.current_best_answer: No scientifically useful absolute minimum is assumed. Minimality is relative to ecology/task class, resource envelope, verification obligations and allowed compilation overhead.
questions.next: Use scoped minimality in all theorem statements.

questions.question: Is state + input + transition + output a novel fundamental unit?
questions.current_best_answer: No. This is strongly parent-owned by automata, coalgebra and dynamical-system formalisms.
questions.next: Identify a developmental/resource residual or kill B0.

questions.question: Must adaptation be inside the primitive itself?
questions.current_best_answer: Not necessarily. A fixed executable morphology can have been produced by an external developmental process. Track B must separate primitive execution semantics from the meta-level update/morphogenesis operator.
questions.next: Stage-C must compare bases with explicit on-unit adaptation versus external update semantics.

questions.question: Is stochasticity fundamental?
questions.current_best_answer: Expressively, stochastic computation can often be related to deterministic computation plus randomness, while probabilistic formalisms provide cleaner semantics. Whether stochastic primitives are resource/learning-irreducible is open.
questions.next: Separate deterministic and explicit-stochastic Stage-C arms and compare bounded compilation.

questions.question: Are warrant, provenance, scope and authority fundamental cognitive-atom fields?
questions.current_best_answer: No evidence establishes this. They may be valuable morphology-level properties under verification/revision ecologies. Baking them into the atom would pre-select OCM.
questions.next: Keep u2 as Cognitive Asset Contract; test whether such fields emerge/become favorable in high-revision/high-verification regimes.

questions.question: Can the same basis represent neural, symbolic, probabilistic and programmatic computation?
questions.current_best_answer: Likely representable for sufficiently universal bases, but representability alone is non-evidence.
questions.next: Known-form micro-derivations with bounded costs and no architecture macros.

questions.question: Can the same basis developmentally acquire those forms without target labels?
questions.current_best_answer: AutoML-Zero gives a strong positive precedent for rediscovering neural learning from primitive operations, but cross-paradigm blind acquisition is not established.
questions.next: Blind tiny known-form recovery after Stage-C grammar freeze.

questions.question: Is there one unique morphogenesis generator Gamma?
questions.current_best_answer: No uniqueness is assumed. Different search/development procedures may generate equivalent frontier distributions.
questions.next: Define generator equivalence by induced developmental-equivalence classes/frontiers.

questions.question: What is the correct unit of morphology identity?
questions.current_best_answer: Current behavior is insufficient; exact witness proves identical behavior can hide different developmental laws. Morphology identity must include development/update and resource behavior.
questions.next: Formalize developmental bisimulation/preorder or explicitly reject equivalence if non-transitive under tolerances.

questions.question: Can known learning laws be unified by one generic U?
questions.current_best_answer: Only trivially. An arbitrary UPDATE(machine, experience) primitive hides the algorithm and collapses Track B to universal computation.
questions.next: Compare structural coordinates of update laws and bounded derivation cost.

questions.question: Why do neural networks dominate many current tasks?
questions.current_best_answer: Candidate contributors include differentiable credit assignment, distributed/shared representation learning, amortization over huge reuse horizons, favorable empirical scaling, and hardware/software co-design. None implies universal dominance.
questions.next: Prospective phase experiments varying reuse horizon, revision frequency and hardware prices.

questions.question: Are neural networks non-developmental?
questions.current_best_answer: No. MAML, learned optimizers, differentiable plasticity, continual learning and topology evolution are direct counterexamples.
questions.next: Use adaptive neural parents, never frozen strawmen.

questions.question: What limits long-lived neural development?
questions.current_best_answer: Plasticity loss is a demonstrated limitation of standard deep continual-learning procedures in broad studied settings; stability/forgetting, retraining economics and exact revision are separate issues.
questions.next: Track plasticity and retention separately in morphology frontiers.

questions.question: Can developmental efficiency be summarized as d(development)/d(cost)?
questions.current_best_answer: Yes only after prospectively choosing a capability utility and resource price vector. Default science should use a Pareto developmental frontier; derivative/finite-difference productivity is secondary.
questions.next: Exact finite phase-frontier calibration before larger empirical use.

questions.question: What variables define a morphology phase diagram?
questions.current_best_answer: Candidate axes include data/noise/smoothness, compositionality, feedback/credit structure, uncertainty, drift, revision, reuse horizon, verification strength and physical hardware prices.
questions.next: Choose small identifiable axis set; prospectively predict frontier reversals.

questions.question: Can one morphology be universally best?
questions.current_best_answer: No unrestricted universal-superiority claim is allowed under NFL/resource-relative considerations. Conditional structured-ecology dominance is the target.
questions.next: State every dominance result with ecology/resource assumptions.

questions.question: Does hardware belong in the intelligence theory?
questions.current_best_answer: Algorithmic identity need not include hardware, but morphology selection/frontier claims must include hardware/resource prices because specialized tensor hardware can strongly alter cost.
questions.next: Run at least one phase analysis under multiple price/hardware models.

questions.question: What would count as a genuinely new form of machine intelligence?
questions.current_best_answer: Not syntax. Candidate must be developmentally and resource distinct from registered known families after simplification and bounded compilation attacks, and preferably be predicted before search.
questions.next: Use U0-U6 evidence ladder in UNKNOWN_MORPHOLOGY_PROGRAMME_V1.

questions.question: Should we launch open-ended morphology search now?
questions.current_best_answer: Not before neutral Stage-C grammar, developmental equivalence, known-form derivations and at least one predictive phase result. Otherwise search will mostly reflect encoding/descriptors.
questions.next: Keep #221/#220 as future search backend only.

questions.question: Can finite search prove open-ended/new intelligence indefinitely?
questions.current_best_answer: Finite trajectories/searches cannot establish unbounded future novelty without stronger transition-law assumptions; open-endedness remains scoped/horizon-based.
questions.next: Use bounded candidate language only.

questions.question: Can Gamma and U themselves become developmental state?
questions.current_best_answer: Conceptually yes, but lower-level parents already cover learned optimizers, architecture search and solver improvement. Track-B residual would require fresh-ecology reduction in complete morphology-acquisition burden or improved phase prediction.
questions.next: META_MORPHOGENESIS_NOT_YET_AUTHORIZED until B2/B3 succeed.

questions.question: Is current OCM the general form of intelligence?
questions.current_best_answer: No. Treat current OCM as one candidate explicit/governed morphology in the space. Track B must permit neural, probabilistic, programmatic, hybrid or unknown forms to dominate.
questions.next: Use OCM only as one morphology target in later phase tests.
